title: Amazon S3 stores objects, not files.
body: Every item in S3 is an object: data, a unique key and some metadata, kept in a bucket. There are no real folders. A slash in a key only looks like one.

title: Git saves snapshots, not lists of changes.
body: Each commit records what the whole project looked like at that moment. A branch is just a light pointer to one commit, which is why branching is so fast.

title: In SQL, NULL is not zero. It means unknown.
body: Comparing a value to NULL with = never gives true. To find missing values, write IS NULL instead of = NULL.

title: AI language models read tokens, not words.
body: Text is split into tokens: whole words, parts of words or single characters. Context limits and prices are usually counted in tokens.

title: Big, close buttons are faster to hit.
body: Fitts's law says the time to reach a target depends on its distance and its size. Make the main action large and keep it close to where the pointer or thumb already is.

title: Spread your app across Availability Zones.
body: An AWS Region is a geographic area. Each Region has several Availability Zones, which are separate groups of data centres. Running in more than one means a single failure does not take you offline.

title: Let the HTTP method say what you want.
body: In a REST API, GET reads, POST creates, PUT replaces, PATCH changes part of a resource and DELETE removes it. The URL names the thing, the method names the action.

title: A good AI prompt has four parts.
body: State the task, give the context the model needs, say who the answer is for, and name the format you want. Vague prompts get vague answers.

title: Use the median when a few values are huge.
body: One very large value drags the mean up but barely moves the median. That is why salaries and house prices are usually reported as medians.

title: Give permissions only where they are needed.
body: This is the principle of least privilege. In AWS IAM, everything is denied unless a policy allows it, and an explicit deny always beats an allow.

title: 401 and 403 are not the same error.
body: 401 means the server does not know who you are, so you need to sign in. 403 means it knows who you are and you are still not allowed.

title: WHERE filters rows. HAVING filters groups.
body: WHERE runs before grouping and works on individual rows. HAVING runs after GROUP BY and works on aggregates such as COUNT or SUM.

title: Text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1.
body: WCAG level AA asks for 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Check your colours with a contrast checker before you ship.

title: What is the difference between a security group and a network ACL in AWS?
body: A security group is stateful, attaches to an instance's network interface and only has allow rules. A network ACL is stateless, applies to a whole subnet and supports both allow and deny rules.

title: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
body: A process has its own memory space. Threads live inside a process and share its memory, so they are lighter but need care when they touch the same data.

title: What is overfitting and how can you reduce it?
body: The model memorises its training data and then does badly on new data. Use more data, a simpler model, regularisation, cross-validation or early stopping.

title: What is a hallucination in a language model and how can you reduce it?
body: A fluent answer that is not true. Give the model trusted sources to answer from, ask it to cite them, keep the question narrow and check important claims yourself.

title: What is the difference between UX and UI design?
body: UX is how the whole experience works and feels: research, flows and usability. UI is the visual layer people touch: layout, type, colour and components.
